questions.problem: Given that $Q(2,4,1)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-6,2,9⟩=5$, find the shortest distance from $P(6,-1,0)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,4,1⟩-⟨6,-1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-6,2,9⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot (-6)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 9|}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{9}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|24+10+9|}{\sqrt{36+4+81}} \\  & =\frac{|43|}{\sqrt{121}} \\  & =\frac{43}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(4,-2,8)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-3,6,2⟩=-8$, find the shortest distance from $P(3,-4,2)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-2,8⟩-⟨3,-4,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,2,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,6,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 6+6\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-3+12+12|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{21}{7} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(3,-4,5)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-2,4,-4⟩=-42$, find the shortest distance from $P(1,-5,2)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨3,-4,5⟩-⟨1,-5,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-2,4,-4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 4+3\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+4-12|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-12|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{12}{6} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,3,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x-3y+6z=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-2$ and $y=0$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-3y+6z & =16 \\ -2(-2)-3(0)+6z & =16 \\ 6z & =12 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-2,0,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-2,0,2⟩-⟨5,3,7⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,-3,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-7)\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot (-3)+(-5)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(6)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|14+9-30|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,3,-6)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-x+2y+2z=8.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-2$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+2y+2z & =8 \\ -1(-2)+2(1)+2z & =8 \\ 2z & =4 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-2,1,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-2,1,2⟩-⟨-2,3,-6⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-1,2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|0\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+8\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|0-4+16|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|12|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{12}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
